title: GE Vernova — Data Archival Portal
oneLiner: Enterprise archival and search platform combining low-cost S3 storage, secure server-side exports, Athena authorization and encrypted-data filtering.
problem: Enterprise project metadata and millions of files needed lower-cost long-term storage while remaining searchable, filterable and securely exportable. Protected data also made conventional direct text filtering unsuitable.
solution: Built Django REST APIs around S3 archival workflows, a Lambda-assisted controlled export path, user-aware Athena filtering, trigram-based search representations for protected values, and paginated OpenSearch APIs for full-text retrieval.
architecture: The export path separates request validation, protected-file retrieval and response streaming: Django receives and authorizes the request, invokes AWS Lambda, Lambda retrieves and decrypts the protected file, and Django streams the resulting bytes to the authorized user without exposing the underlying storage location. For queryable data, Django authorization is carried into Athena so returned rows remain scoped to the authenticated user's access.
security: Implemented a security-focused backend architecture for US/EC export-controlled data: Django validates the user's request, AWS Lambda handles the protected retrieval and decryption step, and Django returns the resulting file bytes to the authorized user. Separating responsibilities keeps protected storage behind the server-side workflow and minimizes direct exposure of the underlying file location. For structured Athena data, user-specific access scope is applied to query results so users cannot retrieve rows outside their permitted scope; the same authorization model is applied to exported and queryable data.
dataStrategy: When conventional text search was not suitable for encrypted or protected values, generated a trigram-based representation for filtering. The representation was indexed and used by the Athena query layer to identify matching records without unnecessarily exposing the original sensitive value to the search path. This made practical filtering more usable across large enterprise datasets while preserving the protected-data boundary.
scale: The platform supported archival workflows across 230 enterprise projects, 6M files and search across 3M encrypted files.

decisions.question: Why combine S3, Athena and OpenSearch?
decisions.answer: The system needed inexpensive durable storage, SQL-style access to structured data with user-specific filtering, and low-friction full-text search for encrypted files.

decisions.question: Why keep export processing behind Django and Lambda?
decisions.answer: The protected file should not be exposed through a storage URL. Request validation, retrieval, decryption and response streaming stay in controlled server-side stages with clear responsibility boundaries.

decisions.question: Why use trigram-based filtering?
decisions.answer: Protected values are difficult to search with conventional direct text matching. A trigram representation gives Athena a searchable index path without making the original sensitive value the search surface.

lessons: The result was an 80% reduction in storage cost while preserving controlled access, secure export behavior and practical search across enterprise-scale protected data. The broader lesson is that application authorization, data-layer filtering and server-side file handling need to be designed together rather than added as isolated features.

title: GE Vernova — Data Access Portal
oneLiner: Django backend for a financial visualization platform with natural-language query workflows and automated report migration.
problem: Analysts needed a faster way to generate structured JSON templates and query cloud datasets, while a large report migration had to happen with minimal manual work.
solution: Built Django REST APIs, SQL-to-JSON translation and validation pipelines, and automated migration scripts for templates and reports.
architecture: Python/Django REST API over SQL-backed cloud datasets, with validation between natural-language-driven query intent and generated JSON structures.

decisions.question: Why automate the migration?
decisions.answer: The migration involved 130+ blank templates and 10,000 associated reports, making scripted transfer more reliable and repeatable than manual movement.

lessons: Query translation is only useful when paired with validation; correctness and predictable output matter as much as generation speed.

title: GE Vernova — Vernova Data Portal
oneLiner: Backend revamp of a legacy enterprise portal around hierarchical domain-based access and embedded analytics.
problem: The legacy portal needed a clearer access model and a modern backend foundation for embedded analytics and chatbot experiences.
solution: Led the backend revamp, established hierarchical domain-based access, and integrated Tableau/Spotfire reports and a custom chatbot through iframes.
architecture: Python/Django REST APIs provide the access-control and application layer while embedded analytics surfaces remain integrated into the portal UI.
lessons: A backend modernization is often as much about defining a clean access model as replacing implementation details.

title: Paradigm My Blogsite
oneLiner: A personal blog where I write about backend engineering, systems, programming and the topics I am learning.
problem: Ideas and engineering notes are easier to revisit and share when they have a consistent home instead of living in scattered drafts.
solution: A dedicated publishing site for structured technical writing, reflections and practical notes across different topics.
architecture: A Next.js publishing experience backed by a separate content system, with the writing kept independent from this portfolio.
lessons: Writing in public is a useful forcing function for turning vague ideas into clear explanations.

title: Daily YouTube Shorts Pipeline
oneLiner: Automated daily pipeline that generates, captions, uploads and publishes YouTube Shorts with GitHub Actions.
problem: Creating and publishing short-form videos repeatedly involves several manual steps: scripting, metadata, captions, uploading and scheduling.
solution: A Gemini-assisted workflow generates a short script, voiceover-ready assets, captions and metadata, then uploads the video through the YouTube API.
architecture: Gemini API → script and metadata generation → video/caption assembly → YouTube API upload, with GitHub Actions scheduling the workflow and repository secrets holding credentials.

decisions.question: Why GitHub Actions?
decisions.answer: The pipeline is batch-oriented and can run once a day without maintaining a dedicated server or local machine.

decisions.question: How are credentials handled?
decisions.answer: API keys, OAuth client details and refresh tokens stay in GitHub Actions secrets rather than the repository.

lessons: Small automation pipelines become dependable when generation, publishing and secret management are explicit stages with clear failure boundaries.

title: This Portfolio
oneLiner: Static Next.js portfolio backed by Django for dynamic contact handling, designed as an evidence-linked engineering document.
problem: A resume lists technologies but rarely shows the reasoning, constraints, or measurable outcomes behind them.
solution: Static-export Next.js serves read-heavy portfolio content cheaply and quickly; Django is reserved for dynamic backend behavior such as contact handling and the future grounded assistant.
architecture: JSON content → static Next.js pages → CDN-friendly output, with a separate Django API for dynamic behavior. Docker provides a repeatable local backend environment.

decisions.question: Why static + Django API?
decisions.answer: Most portfolio content does not change per request, so static delivery is a better fit; Django remains only where server-side behavior adds value.

decisions.question: Why evidence links?
decisions.answer: The portfolio should make technical claims inspectable instead of asking a recruiter or interviewer to take them on faith.

lessons: Content quality comes before the AI assistant: retrieval is only useful when there is real engineering material to ground it on.
